report.summary: In the 'app-183d-events' index (mapping defines service, event_type, duration_ms and timestamp; health green, status open, docs.count 10, store.size 6.3kb), a terms aggregation on the 'service' keyword field filtered on timestamp to the authorized window (time_field=timestamp, 2026-10-24T17:13:37Z to 2026-11-23T17:13:37Z) matched 10 documents in total (relation eq, 1 shard successful, 0 failed) and returned three service buckets: payment-api 5, order-service 3, inventory-api 2, with sum_other_doc_count 0. A size=10 document fetch over the same window returned exactly those 10 documents, all with event_type 'request', timestamps 2026-11-23T15:11:00Z through 2026-11-23T17:12:00Z (source_start_at 2026-11-23T15:11:00Z, source_end_at 2026-11-23T17:12:00Z), matching both the aggregation counts and the index's current docs.count of 10. The requested distribution, as observed in this index, is payment-api 5, order-service 3, inventory-api 2. This is a count of stored event documents, not a statement about service health, request rates or errors.

claims.text: The 'app-183d-events' index exists, is open and green, and held docs.count 10 with store.size 6.3kb at query time; its mapping defines service (keyword), event_type (keyword), duration_ms (integer) and timestamp (date).

A terms aggregation on the service keyword field, filtered on timestamp to the authorized window, matched 10 documents (total relation eq, 1 shard successful, 0 failed) and returned exactly three buckets: payment-api 5, order-service 3, inventory-api 2, with sum_other_doc_count 0.

Fetching the 10 newest documents in the window returned all 10: 5 with service payment-api, 3 with order-service and 2 with inventory-api, every one with event_type 'request', timestamps from 2026-11-23T15:11:00Z to 2026-11-23T17:12:00Z, matching the aggregation bucket counts.

gaps: Two earlier search attempts without time_field returned status error (INVALID_PARAMS, TIME_FIELD_REQUIRED) because the index maps 'timestamp' rather than '@timestamp'; those error views carry no citable evidence_id, so they support no fact. The counts reported come only from the two retried queries that supplied time_field=timestamp.
The aggregation reflects only documents stored in this index whose timestamp falls inside the authorized window; events dropped by retention or ingest delay, or written to another index, are unknown.
All 10 stored documents are timestamped within 2026-11-23T15:11:00Z-17:12:00Z; the index holds no earlier historical samples, so no baseline for comparison exists in this index.

The distribution is stored event-document counts, not request or error rates; no event_type other than 'request' appears in the 10 documents, but services with no stored events cannot be shown, and missing counts for other services are unknown rather than zero.
Integration 'change_history' is not available in this Run, so whether any deployment or configuration change relates to these events is unknown.
next_steps: If per-service event volume over time is needed, query the same index with a date_histogram on timestamp and a terms sub-aggregation on service.
If these events are to be related to service health, cross-check payment-api, order-service and inventory-api against trace and metric sources, since this events index carries no error signal.
